chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Our dye is Al-Bahraman, and the dye of the Banu Umayya is saffron.

key_terms.الْبَهْرَمَانُ: Al-Bahraman (a specific type of dye, often identified as indigo or a dark blue/black dye)
key_terms.صِبْغُنَا: Our dye (referring to the dye preferred by the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred dye for clothing according to the Imams in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith employs a symbolic color contrast to distinguish the spiritual and social identity of the Ahl al-Bayt from the Umayyad caliphs, with 'Al-Bahraman' (a deep blue or indigo) representing humility and 'saffron' signifying the ostentation of the ruling elite. In Shia scholarly tradition, this distinction underscores the concept of *takhalluq* (adornment with moral qualities), where external appearance reflects internal spiritual states and historical lineage.
